conventions.convention: The cell is Λ=Aℤ³ with A invertible, V=|det A|, dual lattice A⁻ᵀℤ³, and angular frequencies κ_k=2πA⁻ᵀk. Fourier coefficients use the negative exponential and the factor 1/V.

Source counts may be zero; charges are real, positions are pairwise distinct on the torus, and neutrality means their sum is zero. The Poisson normalization is −Δu=4πρ with zero Fourier mode fixed to zero.

Energy is one half the charge-weighted regular potential after subtracting each particle's own q_i/r singularity. Ewald real sums omit only the own zero-image term; the energy self constant is −αΣq_i²/√π.

W₁ includes both endpoints of [0,1]; for P≥2 the window is the stated causal truncated-power spline supported on [0,P]. Assignment includes all predecessor support indices and accumulates duplicate wrapped residues.
The mesh transform has negative exponent and normalization N_g⁻¹ᐟ². Causal assignment is deconvolved by conjugate D(k), and z_k=√N_g ĝ_M(k)/conjugate D(k), with no additional volume factor.

Retained modes form a finite symmetric nonzero set, are injective modulo the mesh, and satisfy |k_r|<M_r/2. Even-grid Nyquist modes are excluded, and division requires a certified positive lower bound for |D(k)|.

Physical gradients are A⁻ᵀ times fractional-coordinate gradients. At P=2 knots, the declared derivative is a selected adjacent one-sided vector limit or the average of all such limits, without a classical differentiability claim.

Real and reciprocal radial cutoffs retain distances at most their cutoff. Tail estimates start at the floor of the cutoff; finite force sums hold their cutoff index sets fixed rather than differentiating membership indicators.
Countable Choice is assumed for the screened-kernel and periodic Ewald analysis, including the published divergence, Gaussian-transform, lattice-Poisson, and Fourier-uniqueness interfaces.

Non-transform certificate requests have a finite instruction cap, defaulting to one, and are not retried with larger budgets inside an execution. The evaluator selects the right-hand adjacent box at P=2 knots and returns an explicit status when required comparisons, branches, divisors, or enclosures remain unresolved.

Arithmetic error radii must bound the actual computed finite outputs relative to their exact-real truncated expressions. Formal exact-constant transform work counts exclude interval precision and phase evaluation and supply no numerical accuracy guarantee.

load_bearing.statement: For the periodic cardinal-assignment model with P≥2, signed retained modes |k_r|<M_r/2 and D(k)≠0, b_k(t)=Σ_n r_{k,n}a_{k+n⊙M}(t) and z_k=Σ_n r_{k,n}ρ_{k+n⊙M}, absolutely convergently. Also z_k=Σ_i q_i b_k(t_i), |b_k−a_k|≤A_k, |b_k|≤1+A_k, |z_k−ρ_k|≤QA_k, and the periodic assignment weights sum to one.

Assume Countable Choice. For invertible B, every translate of Bℤ³ has at most C_B(m+1)³ points in shell m≤|z|<m+1. For β>0 and integers p,M≥0, T_p(β,M)≤U_p(β,M,J) whenever J≥M and 2βJ(J+1)≥p; such a J exists.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data with pairwise distinct torus positions. For every α>0, the displayed absolutely convergent off-source Ewald potential represents the unique mean-zero periodic solution of −Δu=4πρ and is independent of α. Its source finite parts exist and are α-independent; their charge-weighted half-sum equals the displayed real-space, reciprocal-space, and self-correction energy formula.

For P≥3, the stated absolutely convergent derivative-alias series and finite p-series controllers give ||∇_x b_k−∇_x a_k||₂≤B_k. For P=2, the finite piecewise-window controller bounds the same error on open mesh boxes and for every declared one-sided knot branch or its allowed average, without asserting classical differentiability at knots.

Under its neutral-data, retained-mode, nonzero-window and derivative-residual hypotheses, the retained mesh potential error is at most QΣ_k c_k A_k(2+A_k), the uncorrected energy error at most Q²Σ_k c_k A_k(2+A_k)/2, and the force error at most |q_i|QΣ_k c_k[|κ_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k]. It also proves the finite transform-gather and cyclic self-correction identities, energy-gradient qualifications, and the stated improved corrected energy and force bounds.

Assume Countable Choice and α>0. The long-range kernel erf(αr)/r extends continuously at zero and has distributional negative Laplacian 4πg_α; erfc(αr)/r has negative Laplacian 4πδ₀−4πg_α, expansion 1/r−2α/√π+O(r²), and the displayed Gaussian bounds for its value and first radial derivative.

Assume Countable Choice. Smooth periodic test functions have absolutely summable Fourier coefficients after multiplication by every derivative-order frequency weight, with Fourier partial sums converging in every smooth seminorm. Every polynomially bounded coefficient sequence defines a continuous periodic distribution by the stated Fourier pairing, and periodic distributions are determined by their Fourier coefficients.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data. The sequence û(0)=0 and û(k)=4πΣ_i q_i exp(−iκ_k·x_i)/(V|κ_k|²) for k≠0 defines the unique mean-zero periodic distribution satisfying −Δu=4πρ.
Assume Countable Choice. For α>0 and every x∈ℝ³, Σ_λ g_α(x+λ)=V⁻¹Σ_k exp(−|κ_k|²/(4α²))exp(iκ_k·x), with absolute and locally uniform convergence of both series.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite source data. For radial cutoffs R,K≥1, the displayed B_R and B_K formulas bound omitted potential, energy, and particle-force tails; replacing T₃ by its finite upper controller preserves the bounds. The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy and equals the displayed real and reciprocal force sums.

Under the stated neutral-data, cutoff, mesh, retained-mode, finite-controller and actual arithmetic-radius hypotheses, |Û(x)−U_α(x)|≤η_U for every off-source x, |Ê^χ−E|≤η_E^χ, and ||F̂_i^χ−F_i||₂≤η_F,i^χ for each particle and either declared correction branch. The displayed radii include real and reciprocal tails, every in-ball omitted mode, retained mesh errors, and arithmetic errors.
